# Implementation Plan: Core JWT Authentication — Open Question Resolutions

**Spec:** `specs/core-jwt-authentication.spec.md`

**Status:** `Approved`
**Plan Author:** Generated by Claude Code

**Target Branch:** `feature/jwt-auth-open-question-resolutions`
**Estimated Effort:** ~4–5 days (1 engineer)

> **Scope note:** `core-jwt-authentication.spec.md` is Approved and its core
> functionality (login, access-token validation, refresh rotation, logout) is
> already implemented — see `src/routes/auth.router.ts`,
> `src/services/token.service.ts`, `src/services/refreshToken.service.ts`,
> `src/services/user.service.ts`. This plan covers **only** the delta
> introduced by the two Open Question resolutions added 2026-07-28, both of
> which were verified against current code as **not yet implemented**:
>
> 1. **Open Question 1** — per-tenant DEK envelope encryption for
>    `users.email` (NFR-6, AC-11, AC-12). Current code derives one global

>    `tenant_encryption_keys` table or `TenantKeyService`.
> 2. **Open Question 2** — client-generated `idempotency_key` on
>    `POST /v1/auth/refresh` (FR-4, AC-10). Current `refreshSchema`,
>    `openapi.yaml`, and `refreshToken.service.ts` have no idempotency-cache
>    logic.
>
> No other FR/AC from the spec is in scope for this plan.

## Phase 1 — API Contract & Data Model

**Goal:** Agree the OpenAPI contract and database schema changes before any service code is written.
**Deliverable:** Reviewed `specs/openapi.yaml` diff + reversible Drizzle migration, no running code yet.

- [ ] **Task 1.1:** Add `idempotency_key` to `RefreshTokenRequest` in `specs/openapi.yaml`
  - Files affected: `specs/openapi.yaml`
  - Change: add optional `idempotency_key` (`type: string`, `format: uuid`) property to the `RefreshTokenRequest` schema component (~line 1563); update the `POST /v1/auth/refresh` operation description to document the 30-second idempotent-retry behavior.
  - Reference: FR-4, AC-10, Zod Schema Changes

- [ ] **Task 1.2:** Add `tenant_encryption_keys` table to `src/db/schema.ts` and generate the migration
  - Files affected: `src/db/schema.ts`, `src/db/migrations/[generated].sql` *(generated by `npm run db:generate` — do not hand-write)*
  - Columns: `tenant_id UUID PK`, `wrapped_dek TEXT NOT NULL`, `key_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`, `created_at`, `rotated_at` — per spec's Data Model Changes.
  - The default-bucket row (for `tenant_id IS NULL` users) is stored under a fixed, well-known sentinel UUID constant, since `tenant_id` is the primary key and cannot itself be `NULL`. Define this sentinel as a named constant (e.g. in `src/services/tenantKey.service.ts`, see Task 2.1) rather than a magic literal repeated at call sites.
  - Reference: NFR-6, Data Model Changes, AC-11, AC-12
  - ⚠️ **Risk:** purely additive (new table, no FK from `users`) — see Risk Register R-3 for the separate cutover concern about *existing* `users.email` rows.

- [ ] **Task 1.3:** Add optional `idempotency_key` to `refreshSchema` in `src/schemas/auth.schemas.ts`
  - Files affected: `src/schemas/auth.schemas.ts`
  - `idempotency_key: z.string().uuid().optional()` on `refreshSchema`, matching `RefreshRequestSchema` in the spec's Zod Schema Changes section and `RefreshTokenRequest` in `openapi.yaml` from Task 1.1.
  - Reference: FR-4, AC-10, Zod Schema Changes

## Phase 2 — Service & Route Implementation

**Goal:** Implement the business logic and HTTP surface conforming to the Phase 1 contract.
**Deliverable:** Per-tenant email encryption and idempotent refresh both functional and unit-tested.

- [ ] **Task 2.1:** Implement `TenantKeyService`
  - Files affected: `src/services/tenantKey.service.ts` (new)
  - Responsibilities: generate + KMS-wrap a DEK per `tenant_id` (local dev: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` as the KEK substitute, per NFR-6); unwrap-and-cache DEKs in a bounded, in-process-only LRU keyed by `tenant_id` (**never Redis or any external store** — spec Implementation Notes); resolve the shared default DEK for the `tenant_id IS NULL` bucket via the sentinel constant from Task 1.2; expose a `rotateTenantKey(tenantId)` method that produces a new wrapped DEK without eagerly re-encrypting existing rows (see Risk Register R-1 — the current `tenant_encryption_keys` schema has no place to retain the pre-rotation DEK, so this method's design needs explicit sign-off before it's built, not a silent assumption).
  - No existing dependency provides a bounded LRU (`lru-cache` is not in `package.json`); default to a small hand-rolled bounded `Map`-based cache unless the reviewer prefers adding the dependency.
  - Reference: NFR-6, AC-11, AC-12, Testing Strategy (`TenantKeyService` row)
  - Depends on: Task 1.2

- [ ] **Task 2.2:** Refactor `src/utils/crypto.ts` for per-tenant DEK resolution
  - Files affected: `src/utils/crypto.ts`
  - `encryptEmail`/`decryptEmail` gain a `tenantId: string | null` parameter and resolve their AES-256-GCM key via `TenantKeyService` instead of the single global `emailEncryptionKey` derived from `ENCRYPTION_KEY`. `hashEmail`/`emailHmacKey` are unchanged — the spec is explicit the HMAC lookup key stays global/unscoped.
  - Reference: NFR-6, AC-11, AC-12
  - Depends on: Task 2.1

- [ ] **Task 2.3:** Update call sites for the new `encryptEmail`/`decryptEmail` signature
  - Files affected: `src/services/user.service.ts` (`decryptEmail(row.email)` → `decryptEmail(row.email, row.tenantId)` in `toAuthenticatedUser`), `tests/helpers/seedUser.ts` (`encryptEmail(input.email)` → pass the fixture's `tenantId`)
  - Note: there is no production `encryptEmail` call site today — no self-registration/insert endpoint exists in this spec's scope — so this task only touches the one `decryptEmail` call site and the test fixture helper.
  - Reference: NFR-6
  - Depends on: Task 2.2

- [ ] **Task 2.4:** Implement the idempotency cache
  - Files affected: `src/services/refreshToken.service.ts` (or alongside the existing Redis helpers in `src/services/token.service.ts`, matching the `revokeToken`/`cacheRefreshTokenRevocation` pattern already there)
  - Key pattern: `idempotency:refresh:<idempotency_key>`, TTL 30s, value = the issued token pair (access + refresh token). Lookup-before-rotate: if a matching key is found, return its cached value unchanged with no DB writes; otherwise proceed with normal rotation/reuse-detection and write the cache entry after a successful rotation.
  - Reference: FR-4, AC-10, Architecture Impact → Redis / cache
  - Depends on: Task 1.3

- [ ] **Task 2.5:** Wire `idempotency_key` through `POST /v1/auth/refresh`
  - Files affected: `src/routes/auth.router.ts`
  - The handler at `authRouter.post('/refresh', ...)` (currently ~line 132) checks the Task 2.4 cache before calling `rotateRefreshToken` when `idempotency_key` is present, and writes to it after issuing a new pair.
  - Reference: FR-4, AC-10
  - Depends on: Task 2.4

- [ ] **Task 2.6:** Unit tests
  - Files affected:
    - `src/services/__tests__/tenantKey.service.test.ts` (new) — generate+wrap DEK, unwrap-cache hit/miss (bounded LRU eviction), default-bucket fallback for `tenant_id IS NULL`, `rotateTenantKey` without re-encrypting existing rows, two tenants' ciphertexts not cross-decryptable
    - `src/utils/__tests__/encryption.test.ts` (update) — per-tenant `encryptEmail`/`decryptEmail` roundtrip, distinct DEKs per tenant
    - `src/schemas/__tests__/validation.test.ts` (update) — `refreshSchema` accepts a well-formed `idempotency_key` UUID and rejects a malformed one
  - Mock `ioredis`/`pg` per project convention; TenantKeyService KMS-wrap calls mocked at the crypto boundary, not `ioredis`.
  - Reference: Testing Strategy (Unit Tests table), AC-10, AC-11, AC-12

- [ ] **Task 2.7:** Integration tests
  - Files affected: `src/__tests__/integration/auth.test.ts` (update)
  - ACs covered: AC-10 (duplicate `idempotency_key` within the 30s window returns the identical pair with no additional `refresh_tokens` row; cache expiry falls back to normal reuse detection), AC-11 (two tenants' `users.email` encrypted under distinct wrapped DEKs recorded in `tenant_encryption_keys`), AC-12 (`tenant_id IS NULL` users share the one default DEK)
  - Uses real Postgres + Redis via Testcontainers — do not mock in integration tests.
  - Depends on: Task 2.5, Task 2.3

## Risk Register

| # | Risk | Severity | Likelihood | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|------|----------|------------|------------|-------|
| R-1 | `tenant_encryption_keys` has one row per `tenant_id` (PK) holding a single `wrapped_dek` + `key_version`. `rotateTenantKey` (Task 2.1) is required to work *without* re-encrypting existing rows (per Testing Strategy), but the spec's data model doesn't define where the pre-rotation DEK is retained once `key_version` increments — decrypting rows encrypted under the old DEK would break. | Medium | Medium (only if/when rotation is actually invoked; no rotation trigger/endpoint is in scope here) | Do not silently assume a design — get explicit sign-off on how the outgoing wrapped DEK stays addressable (e.g. a small key-history table, or a versioned column) before implementing `rotateTenantKey` or writing its unit test in Task 2.6. | Engineer implementing Task 2.1 |
| R-2 | The idempotency cache (Task 2.4) holds a plaintext access+refresh token pair in Redis for ~30s — a new location where live tokens exist outside the client, flagged explicitly in the spec's Implementation Notes. | High if unmitigated | Low (short TTL, single-purpose key) | Mandatory scoped `security-reviewer` pass (Task 3.2) before merge; keep TTL fixed at 30s; never log the cached value; confirm the security reviewer's call on whether to encrypt the cached blob at rest. | Engineer implementing Task 2.4 + security reviewer |
| R-3 | Any `users.email` rows already persisted under the current single global `ENCRYPTION_KEY`-derived scheme become undecryptable once Task 2.2/2.3 switch `decryptEmail` to per-tenant DEK resolution, unless the `tenant_id IS NULL` default-bucket DEK is bootstrapped to remain compatible or those rows are re-encrypted as part of rollout. | Medium | Low today (no production `encryptEmail` call site exists yet — only test fixtures) but High for any environment with real pre-existing rows | Confirm before deploying to any environment with real users: either (a) no live rows exist yet, or (b) run a one-time backfill re-encrypting existing rows under the new default DEK as part of this change's rollout, before the old global-key code path is removed. | Engineer implementing Task 2.2, deploy owner |
| R-4 | Per-tenant DEK cache is in-process/per-instance only (never Redis, per spec) — every gateway instance independently performs a KMS-unwrap on first use per tenant after a restart or scale-out event. | Low | Medium (routine on deploys/autoscale) | Size the LRU generously for the active tenant working set; watch decrypt-path latency against NFR-1 (P95 ≤150ms) after rollout. | Engineer implementing Task 2.1 |

## Rollback Plan

### Trigger Conditions

Roll back if any of the following occur after deployment:
- [ ] Email decrypt failures spike on `/v1/auth/login` or `/v1/auth/me` (symptom of R-3 — a compatibility gap for pre-existing rows)
- [ ] P95 latency on `/v1/auth/login`, `/v1/auth/refresh`, or `/v1/auth/me` exceeds the NFR-1 budget (150ms) attributable to DEK unwrap cache misses (R-4)
- [ ] Duplicate or incorrect token pairs observed from `/v1/auth/refresh` under the same `idempotency_key` (idempotency cache bug)

### Rollback Steps

**Application:**
1. Revert the PR / redeploy the previous image tag — this reverts `crypto.ts`, `tenantKey.service.ts`, `refreshToken.service.ts`, and `auth.router.ts` together as one deployable unit, so the code and schema stay consistent (avoids a mixed state where new code expects the new table but old code is running, or vice versa).

**Database:**
- Migration rollback: `tenant_encryption_keys` is a new, standalone table with no foreign key from `users` — dropping it is safe and reversible (`DROP TABLE tenant_encryption_keys;`) as long as the application code has already been rolled back first (drop the table only after Task "Application" step 1 above).
- ⚠️ **Data impact:** if any `users.email` row was re-encrypted under a tenant/default DEK before rollback (see R-3 mitigation), rolling back to the old global-key `decryptEmail` will fail to decrypt those specific rows. Confirm no such re-encryption backfill has run, or restore the pre-rollout `email` ciphertext from a backup, before rolling back in an environment with real data.
